output.reason: On its own, the cited item [ev-61d6d2b50a95] is just "- app", but the section it comes from explains what it means. [ev-b07a4021f30c] says Loki 3.0 now adds a `service_name` label to every ingested log by default. Loki takes the value from the first label it finds in a fixed order: service_name, service, app, application, and so on through job [ev-92063a2a5bac, ev-2690c7915f58, ev-61d6d2b50a95, ev-c8bbef5b1d06, ev-ea984d665a12]. If none of those labels is present, the value is `unknown_service`; operators can change the list, or turn the feature off with an empty value, using `discover_service_name` in limits_config. So "app" is the third entry in the new default lookup list. That is enough to write the assertion: the subject is the new default service_name label assignment and its `discover_service_name` default, the change is that this behavior is added and on by default, exposure is logs ingested into 3.0 that don't already carry `service_name`, and the consequence is that those streams get an extra `service_name` label. This "app" item is one entry of that larger change rather than a separate change.
